title: MCP Integration
description: The boot service ships with an MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Other agents can generate memory shells and echo/probe shells on the server through its tools.
endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.hint: The endpoint follows the current deployment address and keeps any reverse-proxy path prefix; Jar and Docker deployments default to http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp.
tools.title: Tools
tools.capabilities.description: Lists every supported server, shell tool, shell type, packer, probe method, obfuscation option and obfuscation scope.
tools.memshell.description: Generates a memory shell on the server and returns memShellResult and packResult; the request matches POST /api/memshell/generate (Godzilla, Behinder, AntSword, Suo5, Command, etc.).
tools.probe.description: Generates an echo/probe shell on the server and returns probeShellResult and packResult; the request matches POST /api/probe/generate (DNSLog, ResponseBody, ResponseHeader, Sleep).
clients.title: Connect a client
clients.description: Examples for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Claude Desktop; any other Streamable HTTP client works with the same endpoint.
clients.authPending: Checking authentication. The examples below do not include credentials yet.
clients.authError: Could not check authentication. The examples below are unauthenticated. Reload and sign in again if ADMIN authentication is enabled.
clients.adminStatus: ADMIN authentication is enabled. These configurations include your current Basic credential. Keep it secret. Direct REST API calls need the same Authorization header.
clients.platformStatus: PLATFORM authentication is enabled. Configure the platform credential in your client. These examples do not include it.
clients.desktopHint: Claude Desktop only supports stdio, so bridge it through mcp-remote (requires Node.js).
clients.restartHint: Restart the client after saving the configuration.
workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.step1: Call memshell_capabilities first to discover valid server, shellTool, shellType and packer values.
workflow.step2: Call generate_memshell or generate_probe_shell; generation runs on the server.
workflow.step3: The tool result contains packResult with memShellResult or probeShellResult; no follow-up REST request is needed.
workflow.step4: Save packResult to a file if needed, or use it directly in the injection step.
workflow.examplePrompt: Call memshell_capabilities first for valid parameters, then call generate_memshell to generate a Tomcat + Godzilla Filter memory shell, and read the class names and packResult from the result.
security: For authorized security testing and research only.
